title: AST–ALT coupling adds no established CRP prediction benefit beyond nonlinear enzyme levels and their ratio
abstract: In NHANES2007–2008 (source n=4707) and separately sampled2009–2010 (target n=5028), adding standardized log-AST×log-ALT to a nonlinear standard-marker baseline reduced target log-CRP MSE by 0.0001956 (0.017%;95% joint source-refit/target PSU bootstrap interval -0.0033731 to 0.0012007). This does not establish improvement. A post-primary algebraic self-check showed that the proposed term is already in the span of additive cubic splines of log-AST, log-ALT and log(AST/ALT): 2ab=a²+b²−(a−b)². On5027 target records within source enzyme/ratio support, unpenalized predictions agreed within2.1e−13. The tiny ridge gain reflects parameterization/penalty, not an added model dimension. This negative predictive test does not refute liver–inflammation biology or establish clinical equivalence. Transfer is between survey cross-sections, not independent external cohorts. AI-authored and author-self-checked; no independent peer review claimed.
